messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify buffer_trim_right does not modify a buffer with no trailing whitespace.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures that the function is a no-op when the buffer ends with a non-whitespace character, which is a key boundary case and guards against off-by-one or accidental truncation bugs.

expected_branches: while ((c = self->data[i]) && isspace(c)) → false on first check

dependencies.name: buffer_length
dependencies.reason: Used to determine buffer length for trimming logic

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_content
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer content matches expected string after trimming

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_length
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer string length is unchanged after trimming

utilities.name: helper_create_buffer_with_content
utilities.purpose: Create a buffer initialized with a given string

preconditions: Buffer contains a null-terminated string with no trailing whitespace
setup_requirements.initial_state: A buffer containing the string 'abc' (no trailing whitespace), properly null-terminated and allocated.

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Buffer with content 'abc' and no trailing whitespace
primary_function_args.rationale: Ensures the function does not trim or modify a buffer that ends with a non-whitespace character.

return_value.description: No return value; buffer is unmodified

invariants_maintained: No bytes after the string are modified

assertions_required.description: Buffer content is unchanged after trimming
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Function incorrectly modified buffer with no trailing whitespace

assertions_required.description: Buffer string length is unchanged after trimming

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All allocated memory freed; no resource leaks

edge_cases_to_note: Buffer with length 1 and no whitespace
Buffer with embedded whitespace but not at end (e.g., 'a b c')

path_coverage_analysis.description: No trailing whitespace: loop exits immediately, buffer unchanged

integration_test_suggestions: Test buffer_trim_right on buffer with only whitespace
Test buffer_trim_right on buffer with trailing whitespace
